newsitem.title: USA: Fox, Time Warner agree on retransmission.
newsitem.headline: Fox, Time Warner agree on retransmission.

text.p: News Corp's Fox Network said on Wednesday it reached an agreement under which Time Warner Cable's cable systems are allowed to continue retransmitting Fox programming from New World Communications Group television stations.
Time Warner Cable, a unit of Time Warner Inc, retransmits Fox programming in the cities the New World stations are located: Tampa, Fla., Milwaukee, Wis., Austin, Texas, Detroit and Kansas City, Mo.
The two companies have been involved in a legal dispute over Time Warner Cable's right to retransmit Fox's programming from New World stations, which Fox is buying.

Time Warner maintained these stations were covered under an existing agreement that specifies how much compensation Time Warner paid networks it carried on its cable systems, Fox said. But Fox said the stations were not covered under the agreement and filed a lawsuit. It said specific terms of the disputed agreement were confidential.
Either company could terminate the retransmission right on 45-day notice, Fox said, raising the possibility the agreement was only a temporary resolution to the dispute.
Fox said it believed its legal position over the contract dispute was supportable and it would prevail in the pending legal proceedings.
